name: Xcel Energy Inc.
summary:
BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Xcel Energy's AI-load story is real but contractually gated. It has roughly 2 GW of data-center load contracted or under construction against a pipeline it states at more than 20 GW, and the instruments that decide whether that load pays for itself — the Colorado and Wisconsin large-load tariffs and the Google Clean Energy Accelerator Charge — are all pending commission decisions in early 2027; only Minnesota's tariff is approved. It has already reserved the equipment (five GE Vernova F-class turbines within twelve gas-turbine reservations, ten Siemens Energy turbines, multi-gigawatt wind reservations, a 2 GW NextEra joint development agreement) and 85 percent of the $7 billion equity the $60 billion base plan needs. The one unbounded number is wildfire: Marshall closed at $640 million, but Smokehouse Creek stands at a $503 million estimate the company says it cannot cap, with a Texas Attorney General suit set for trial in April 2027.

BACKGROUND. Xcel Energy is a Minneapolis-based holding company for four regulated utilities — Northern States Power-Minnesota (MN, ND, SD), Northern States Power-Wisconsin (WI, MI), Public Service Company of Colorado and Southwestern Public Service (TX, NM) — serving 3.9 million electric and 2.2 million natural-gas customers in eight states with about 21 GW of owned generation and a 2025 rate base of about $56 billion, per the July 2026 Investor Fact Book. 2025 operating revenue was $14.67 billion, ongoing EPS $3.80 (the twenty-first consecutive year inside guidance, per the company), and the 2026–2030 base capital plan is $60 billion with a stated $10 billion-plus of additional line of sight. Carbon emissions are down 58 percent from 2005 per the 2025 Sustainability Report; the company plans to be out of coal by the end of 2030. Listed on Nasdaq as XEL.
ecosystemRole: We assess Xcel Energy as the utility whose value to this ecosystem is the tariff design rather than the megawatts: it is the first utility to put a hyperscaler's full incremental cost — 1,400 MW of wind, 200 MW of solar and a 300 MW / 30 GWh iron-air battery — into a customer-specific charge (the Google Clean Energy Accelerator Charge) and to file large-load tariffs in three states with published minimum-demand, term and exit-fee parameters. For suppliers, the actionable fact is that generation and turbine supply have been reserved at the alliance level (GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, NextEra) ahead of project awards, so entry runs through those partners or through the Colorado, Upper Midwest and SPS all-source solicitations. Collection gap: the company states that further supply-chain partnerships exist but are undisclosed for confidentiality, so the supplier map below is necessarily incomplete.

productsAndServices.name: Regulated electric service — four operating companies, eight states
productsAndServices.description: Vertically integrated electric service through NSP-Minnesota (1.6 million electric customers, ~8,700 MW owned capacity, $19.4 billion 2025E rate base), Public Service Company of Colorado (1.6 million, ~6,500 MW, $23.8 billion), Southwestern Public Service (0.4 million, ~5,100 MW, $9.1 billion) and NSP-Wisconsin (0.3 million, ~500 MW, $3.5 billion), per the July 2026 Investor Fact Book and the May 2026 AGA investor deck. System retail sales were 94,168 GWh in 2025 with 3,894,997 retail electric customers at year-end.
highlights: 2025 ongoing EPS by company: NSP-Minnesota $1.53, PSCo $1.53, SPS $0.67, NSP-Wisconsin $0.27, holding company $(0.23) — per the year-end 2025 earnings deck and Fact Book

Rate base $56 billion in 2025 rising to $94 billion in 2030, a stated ~11 percent CAGR; SPS ~22 percent, NSP-Wisconsin ~13 percent, NSP-Minnesota ~10 percent, PSCo ~7 percent — per the Q2 2026 earnings presentation

Recovery runs through riders as much as base rates: transmission, renewable energy, natural-gas infrastructure and environmental riders plus forward test years with interim rates in Minnesota and North Dakota — per the Fact Book; the 2025 ongoing EPS bridge credits non-fuel riders with +$0.33 against +$0.15 from rate cases

2026 rate-case outcomes cut deep: Colorado electric approved at ~$157 million against a $356 million request (August 2026); Minnesota electric ~$211 million over two years at a 9.6 percent ROE on a 3–2 vote now under reconsideration petitions from the Attorney General — per the Q2 2026 8-K, the Colorado PUC and Energy and Policy Institute
Weather-adjusted retail electric sales growth, 2026 year to date: SPS 4.8 percent, NSP-Minnesota 2.0 percent, NSP-Wisconsin 1.8 percent, PSCo (0.1) percent, total 2.1 percent — per the Q2 2026 deck
productsAndServices.positioning: Against the other utilities in this corpus, Xcel is the one with no single dominant jurisdiction: Dominion and Southern each depend on one commission for most of their load story, while Xcel's data-center growth is spread across the Minnesota PUC (tariff approved), the Colorado PUC (tariff and Just Transition Solicitation pending) and the Texas and New Mexico commissions (SPS, no large-load tariff on file). Analyst comparisons put its 6–8 percent-plus EPS growth objective alongside WEC (7–8 percent) and Alliant (5–7 percent-plus), per an Investing.com summary of a Barclays note.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct, as the franchised utility in each service territory under state-commission-approved tariffs; wholesale sales for resale (15,233 GWh in 2025) and MISO/SPP market participation
productsAndServices.roadmap: Colorado gas decision Q4 2026 (settlement ~$123 million, 9.2 percent ROE); New Mexico electric decision Q4 2026 with rates in December (stipulation ~$90 million, 9.5 percent ROE); Minnesota gas decision November 2026; Minnesota electric written order and reconsideration ruling (PUC response due mid-October 2026); North Dakota gas schedule to be set — per the Q2 2026 8-K and the Minnesota Reformer

productsAndServices.name: Large-load service framework — Minnesota (approved), Colorado and Wisconsin (filed)
productsAndServices.description: The contractual terms on which data centers and other very large customers take service. Minnesota's Large Load Tariff (Proceeding M-25-289) is approved and applies at 100 MW and above; Colorado's (Proceeding 26AL-0137E, filed April 2, 2026) applies at 50 MW with 20–50 MW customers potentially subject; Wisconsin's (4220-TE-119, filed June 22, 2026) applies at 100 MW. All three carry 15-year minimum terms, minimum demand charges (75 percent in Minnesota and Wisconsin, 80 percent in Colorado), collateral, incremental-cost tests and an exit fee equal to the minimum bill times the lesser of the remaining term or ten years — per the Q2 2026 earnings presentation and the company's state information sheets.
highlights: Pipeline as the company states it: ~2 GW contracted or under construction, ~4 GW contracted by year-end 2027, more than 20 GW of additional pipeline; 'Expect ~1 GW signed in 2026' — Q2 2026 deck
Disclosed contracts on the same slide: 200 MW (online, full ramp 2035), 250 MW (online, full ramp 2035), 200 MW (online 2027, ramp 2028), 600 MW (online 2026, ramp 2029), plus undisclosed

Company-stated economics: a 1,000 MW 24/7 contract requires $6–8 billion of investment and produces $0.9–1.3 billion a year of incremental revenue with 'up to 10 percent' savings for other customers — September 2025 investor presentation; CEO Frenzel on the Q2 2026 call: '$5 billion to $6 billion' per gigawatt per the Motley Fool transcript
Minnesota's 2025 law adds annual fees of $2–5 million per large customer, scaled to peak demand, into an income-qualified efficiency account — company information sheet 26-07-237

Colorado's filing drew an Earthjustice-led intervention (May 2026) and resident pushback reported by CPR (August 2026); the Colorado Office of the Utility Consumer Advocate called it 'a good framework' — Colorado Sun, April 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: Colorado's 50 MW threshold and 80 percent minimum demand are the strictest of Xcel's three filings; Georgia Power's PSC rule (100 MW, per the Southern Company dossier) and Dominion Virginia's GS-5 class are the corpus comparators. Xcel's distinguishing move is pairing the tariff with an optional Clean Transition Tariff and the customer-funded CEAC structure, so the clean-energy premium is charged to the load rather than socialized.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct Electric Service Agreements (ESAs) filed with and approved by the state commission; Minnesota ESAs above the threshold require PUC approval
targetSegments: Campuses from 200 MW to 1 GW-plus; urban sites of 10–20 MW also in the pipeline per the Q2 2026 call
productsAndServices.roadmap: Colorado PUC decision expected early 2027 (the company's slide) — third-party reporting says by year-end 2026; Wisconsin PSC decision early 2027; Google ESA and CEAC decision early 2027 after a comment period closing September 8, 2026 — per the Q2 2026 deck, Colorado Sun and Renewables Now

productsAndServices.name: Google Pine Island package — Electric Service Agreement plus Clean Energy Accelerator Charge
productsAndServices.description: A February 2026 agreement under which NSP-Minnesota serves Google's Pine Island, Minnesota data center and adds 1,900 MW of new resources — 1,400 MW of wind, 200 MW of solar and 300 MW of long-duration storage including a 300 MW / 30 GWh Form Energy iron-air battery — recovered from Google through a Clean Energy Accelerator Charge, with Google also funding $50 million of the Capacity*Connect distributed-storage program and paying all new grid infrastructure costs, per the company's February 23–24, 2026 releases.
highlights: Filed with the Minnesota PUC in April 2026; the company states 'approximately $1.1 billion of benefits' to NSP-Minnesota customers if approved — Q1 and Q2 2026 earnings releases
The iron-air unit would be the largest battery in the world by gigawatt-hours, per Renewable Energy World; Form Energy already has a 10 MW / 1,000 MWh pilot at Sherco approved in 2023
CEO Frenzel described the deal as the template for the large-load tariff strategy — Utility Dive, May 2026
Google is contributing $25 million to a Pine Island community fund per the company's July 2026 data-center information sheet
productsAndServices.positioning: The first hyperscaler contract in this corpus to recover a named clean-energy build from one customer outside a resource plan; Latitude Media frames it as the maturing of Google's clean transition tariff concept. Its approval test is whether the Minnesota PUC accepts 1,900 MW on one contract.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct ESA with Echo Zone, LLC (a Google subsidiary), subject to Minnesota PUC approval
productsAndServices.roadmap: Minnesota PUC comment period open until September 8, 2026; decision expected early 2027 — per the Q2 2026 8-K and Renewables Now

productsAndServices.name: Generation build program — 2026–2030 base plan and the three state solicitations
productsAndServices.description: The base plan adds ~11,400 MW of renewable generation, ~3,400 MW of natural gas and ~2,200 MW of storage plus ~1,700 new transmission miles within the $60 billion 2026–2030 plan, with in-service capacity of ~2,100 MW in 2026, ~2,640 MW in 2027, ~3,815 MW in 2028 and ~2,840 MW across 2029–2030; the incremental plan adds a further 2,000 MW wind, 1,900 MW solar, 400 MW gas and 300 MW storage — per the Q2 2026 earnings presentation. Procurement runs through three vehicles: Colorado's Near-Term Procurement and Just Transition Solicitation, the Upper Midwest Energy Plan and SPS's all-source RFPs.
highlights: Colorado Near-Term Procurement: ~3,800 MW approved in April 2026 (wind 1,200 MW, solar 500 MW, hybrid solar 600 MW, hybrid storage 600 MW, storage 700 MW, gas 200 MW; 11 projects, 2 company-owned / 9 PPAs), framed by the company as capturing '$3 billion in federal tax benefits' before credits expire — company information sheet 26-04-628; the PUC's February 18, 2026 release described up to 4,100 MW

Upper Midwest Energy Plan approved February 20, 2025: 3,430 MW wind, 550 MW solar, 600 MW storage by 2030 plus 300 MW lithium-ion at Sherco and the 420 MW Lyon County gas peaker; all coal retired by 2030 — company release and Minnesota PUC bulletin

SPS: July 2025 portfolio of 521 MW of plant extensions plus 17 projects / 5,168 MW by 2030; second portfolio of 3,928 MW (5 solar, 1 solar+storage, 4 wind, 1 gas) filed July 27, 2026; ~2,600 MW recommended as company-owned (~70 percent of the selected portfolio) — company releases and Q2 2026 deck

Company-owned flagships: Sherco Solar 710 MW complete July 2026 (Phase 4 to 910 MW by 2029); Sherco 600 MW and Blue Lake 135.5 MW batteries in service late 2027; High Plains Solar + BESS 250 MW / 200 MW, $685 million, December 2027, built with Mortenson; Cheyenne Ridge 2 (450 MW), Singing Grass (603 MW) and Towner (500 MW) wind CPCNs approved September 2025

Colorado Just Transition Solicitation: Phase 1 approved November 2025 (the PUC's summary cites ~6,000 MW of new generation for 2029–2033 and Comanche 3's retirement by January 1, 2031); Phase 2 RFP launched August 2026 with a report due early 2027
productsAndServices.positioning: Ownership share is the variable to watch: Colorado's NTP split 2 owned / 9 PPA, while SPS's recommendation is ~70 percent company-owned and the Upper Midwest plan carries build-own-transfer wind RFPs (1,200 MW for 2028). The Colorado Sun and Denver Gazette both reported the PUC approving the NTP while 'wary about costs'.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Rate-based self-build, build-own-transfer and PPAs selected through commission-supervised all-source solicitations with independent evaluators
targetSegments: Retail load across the four operating companies
Contracted large-load customers under the CEAC and large-load tariffs
productsAndServices.roadmap: NSP renewable RFP recommendation (~4,100 MW by 2030) filing Q3 2026; SPS CCNs for the 2026 portfolio late 2026 or early 2027; Colorado JTS Phase 2 report early 2027 and PSCo JTS RFP for 2027–2031 needs in Q4 2026; SPS 2025 all-source RFP CODs December 2029 to June 2032 — per the Q2 2026 deck and company RFP pages

productsAndServices.name: Transmission programs — Colorado's Power Pathway, Minnesota Energy Connection and the first 765 kV in SPP
productsAndServices.description: Electric transmission is the largest capex category ($15.44 billion of the $60 billion base plan). Colorado's Power Pathway is ~550 miles of new double-circuit 345 kV at $1.7 billion enabling more than 5,000 MW of renewables; Minnesota Energy Connection is a 175–185 mile 345 kV line from the Sherco hub to Lyon County connecting up to 4,000 MW; Potter–Crossroads–Phantom is the first 765 kV line in the SPP footprint, from Amarillo into southeastern New Mexico — per the company's transmission project pages and releases.
highlights: Power Pathway segments 2 and 3 in service 2025 ('four months ahead of schedule'), segments 1 and 4 in 2026, segment 5 in 2027 — company project page; Colorado cities challenged its cost allocation at FERC per Utility Dive
Minnesota Energy Connection: MPUC approval April 11, 2025, construction kicked off August 3, 2026 alongside the Lyon County peaker, energized 2028 — company releases

'Awarded over 760 miles of new 765 kV transmission in MISO and SPP' (Q4 2025 deck); MISO Tranche 2.1 awards of $1–2 billion and ~$2 billion of the SPP 2024 ITP portfolio (Q2 2025 deck); the PowerOn Midwest 765 kV backbone with Great River Energy and ITC Midwest has a certificate-of-need application filed in Minnesota

Mankato–Mississippi River (~120 miles 345 kV) approved February 2026; Western Wisconsin Transmission Connection (~80 miles 345 kV, MISO Tranche 1) approved November 2025 for 2029; Beckham County–Potter 345 kV with Transource ($222 million, 128 miles, November 2029)
Crawfish Draw–Phantom 765 kV (~$2 billion) sits in the line-of-sight capital, not the base plan — Q2 2026 deck
productsAndServices.positioning: Xcel is building the interregional backbone in both of its RTOs at once — 765 kV in SPP (in service Q2 2031) and MISO's LRTP tranches — which is what makes its 20 GW-plus data-center pipeline physically plausible in a way single-state utilities cannot claim.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Rate-based transmission recovered through FERC formula rates and state transmission riders; multi-utility joint projects for MISO tranche lines
targetSegments: Regional load in MISO and SPP
Renewable interconnection (Power Pathway, Minnesota Energy Connection)
Large-load customers whose gen-ties and substations are funded under the large-load tariffs
productsAndServices.roadmap: Potter–Crossroads–Phantom routing 2025–2028, construction Q1 2029–Q2 2031 (Segment 2 CCN filed with the PUCT June 12, 2026); Fargo–Alexandria second circuit ~2032; PowerOn Midwest 765 kV in service 2032–2034 — company project pages, Great River Energy

productsAndServices.name: Nuclear fleet — Monticello and Prairie Island
productsAndServices.description: Three units totaling ~1,650 MW: Monticello (617 MW, licensed by the NRC to 2050 in January 2025) and Prairie Island units 1 and 2 (521 MW and 519 MW, licenses expiring 2033 and 2034, with a 20-year subsequent renewal application planned for 2026). The fleet supplies 27 percent of Upper Midwest customers' electricity at a >90 percent capacity factor and ~$29/MWh production cost — per the company's Minnesota nuclear information sheet and releases.
highlights: Federal nuclear production tax credits are passed through to customers: $176 million within a $318 million Minnesota refund (March 2025), $25 million to the Dakotas (June 2025), more than $130 million in 2026 and $330 million over two years — 'created under 2022 federal law; continued under 2025 law' per the March 31, 2026 release
Minnesota PUC unanimously approved Prairie Island spent-fuel storage expansion August 14, 2025; the state approval for Monticello runs to 2040 against the NRC's 2050
No SMR or new-nuclear announcement on first-party channels in 2024–2026; the only public link is a 2021-era NuScale operator MOU per ANS — collection gap on Xcel's new-nuclear intent
productsAndServices.positioning: The Upper Midwest's only nuclear operator and the anchor of Minnesota's 100 percent carbon-free-by-2040 compliance path; nuclear is 7 percent of rate base per the Fact Book.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Rate-based generation serving NSP-Minnesota and NSP-Wisconsin retail load
productsAndServices.roadmap: Prairie Island NRC subsequent license renewal application in Q4 2026 (18–24 month review) — company release and World Nuclear News

productsAndServices.name: Natural gas delivery — 2.2 million customers
productsAndServices.description: Gas distribution through NSP-Minnesota (0.6 million customers, 16.9 Bcf storage), PSCo (1.5 million, 32.1 Bcf, 24,000 miles of lines) and NSP-Wisconsin (0.1 million, 4.3 Bcf); $3.72 billion of the base plan is natural gas — per the Fact Book and the company's May 2026 Colorado customer letter.
highlights: Colorado gas rate case: $190 million requested (December 2025), settled July 2026 at ~$123 million with a 9.2 percent ROE, decision Q4 2026; Minnesota gas settled May 2026 at ~$38 million — Q2 2026 8-K

Decarbonization products: Colorado Clean Heat Plan (2024–2027), Minnesota Natural Gas Innovation Plan, and the $155 million Mountain Energy Project non-pipeline alternative for four Colorado mountain counties (January 2025 release)
Company goal of net-zero methane gas service by 2030 per the AGA deck
productsAndServices.positioning: The gas business is the smallest capex line and the one facing the company's own stated safe-harbor risk of 'regulatory changes and/or limitations related to the use of natural gas as an energy source'.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct franchised gas distribution under state tariffs
targetSegments: Residential and commercial gas customers in Minnesota, Colorado, Wisconsin, North Dakota and Michigan
productsAndServices.roadmap: Colorado gas decision Q4 2026; Minnesota gas ALJ report September 2026 and PUC decision November 2026 — Q2 2026 8-K

productsAndServices.name: Wildfire mitigation and Public Safety Power Shutoffs — Colorado and Texas programs
productsAndServices.description: Colorado's 2025–2027 Wildfire Mitigation Plan (~$1.9 billion capital and O&M, approved June 2025) and the Texas System Resiliency Plan (~$495 million, PUCT-approved settlement 2025), with a system-wide ~$5 billion for wildfire mitigation in the 2026–2030 plan, per the AGA investor deck. Both plans formalize PSPS, and the company executed multiple shutoffs in Colorado, Texas and New Mexico in 2025–2026.
highlights: Colorado plan scope: 50 miles undergrounding, 165 miles small-conductor replacement, 10,000 poles, 82,000 overhead defect remediations, 300 EPSS reclosers, 135 AI cameras; securitization mechanism for up to $1.2 billion; ~$9 a month bill impact toward the end of the period per CBS Colorado

Texas: 16,000 poles, 783 miles of conductor, 151 EPSS feeders, 68 AI cameras, 110 weather stations; a $113 million Texas Energy Fund grant (July 2026); a formal SPS Wildfire Mitigation Plan filed with the PUCT August 4, 2026 under a 180-day review

The February 2026 agreed injunction in the Texas AG suit separately requires no fewer than 35,000 pole inspections a year and tiered replacement deadlines (24 hours / 5 days / 35 days) with monthly compliance reports — Utility Dive

Largest PSPS events: Front Range December 16–21, 2025 (~58,000 customers restored by December 21) and the Texas Panhandle February 16–18, 2026 (11,700 customers) — company releases; Colorado PUC PSPS rulemaking hearing January 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: Insurance and legislation, not hardware, distinguish Xcel's wildfire posture: the company credits tort-reform wins in Texas, North Dakota and South Dakota and has no equivalent in Colorado, where its answer is securitization.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Rate-based through the Colorado Wildfire Mitigation Adjustment rider (semiannual) and a Texas deferral mechanism
targetSegments: PSCo and SPS customers in high-fire-risk zones
productsAndServices.roadmap: PUCT decision on the SPS Wildfire Mitigation Plan within 180 days of August 2026; planned 2029 Colorado securitization; Colorado PUC PSPS rules — company deck and releases

productsAndServices.name: Customer-side capacity and flexibility — Capacity*Connect, virtual power plants, demand response and EV programs
productsAndServices.description: Capacity*Connect is a first-in-the-nation distributed capacity procurement: up to 200 MW of company-owned batteries at host sites (1–3 MW each) by end-2028 with Sparkfund, phase 1 of 3–5 MW in 2025–26; Colorado's Renewable Battery Connect virtual power plant enrolls Tesla Powerwall and Enphase batteries on Itron's platform; business demand response pays $1.35/kWh credits under Peak Partner Rewards — per company releases and information sheets.
highlights: Minnesota PUC approved the utility-owned 200 MW / $430 million battery program April 6, 2026 over solar-industry opposition — Utility Dive
Google's ESA routes $50 million into Capacity*Connect
EV: ~730 public fast-charging stations (~1,470 ports, 194 MW) planned in Minnesota by 2026; New Mexico EV Charging Perks launched October 2025; goal of 1.5 million EVs enabled by 2035
2025: $175 million in rebates and incentives, 1,100 GWh saved, $181 million of energy assistance — 2025 Sustainability Report release
productsAndServices.positioning: Distributed capacity is being treated as a rate-base asset class rather than a third-party service, which is why the solar industry objected in Minnesota.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility-owned programs approved by state commissions; residential VPP enrollment through Tesla and Enphase apps
productsAndServices.roadmap: Capacity*Connect phase 2 of 50–200 MW in 2026–2028 — company information sheet 25-10-208

recentDevelopments.headline: Minnesota Attorney General Ellison and the Citizens Utility Board file reconsideration petitions against the PUC's 3–2 verbal decision granting NSP-Minnesota ~$211 million over two years at a 9.6 percent ROE; the PUC's response is due mid-October
recentDevelopments.read: The commission that approved Xcel's large-load tariff is the same one now being asked to reopen its base-rate ROE — the Google decision in early 2027 arrives into a contested record.

recentDevelopments.headline: CPR reports resident and advocate pushback on Xcel's Colorado large-load tariff (Proceeding 26AL-0137E), following an Earthjustice-led intervention in May
recentDevelopments.read: Colorado's tariff is the strictest of the three Xcel has filed and is still the one drawing opposition — the fight is over whether 'full incremental cost' is enforceable, not over the threshold.

recentDevelopments.headline: Colorado PUC approves a ~$157 million electric rate increase against a $356 million request and a $225 million settlement (Proceeding 25AL-0494E); Commissioner Eric Blank warns about capital spending 'considerably faster than inflation'
recentDevelopments.read: A 56 percent haircut on a settled case is the clearest signal yet that PSCo's ~7 percent rate-base CAGR is the ceiling the commission will tolerate through base rates.

recentDevelopments.headline: SPS files a Wildfire Mitigation Plan with the Texas PUC under a 180-day review; Brad Baldridge is quoted as interim president, Xcel Energy – Texas
recentDevelopments.read: The first formal Texas plan under the state's new framework — and the release confirms that SPS has been run by an interim president since March 2026 with no explanatory announcement.

recentDevelopments.headline: Construction begins on the 185-mile Minnesota Energy Connection (up to 4,000 MW of renewables) and the 420 MW Lyon County Generating Station; both complete in 2028
recentDevelopments.read: The physical anchor of the Upper Midwest coal-replacement plan is now in the ground; the wind that fills the line is still to be procured through the ~4,100 MW NSP RFP.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q2 2026: ongoing EPS $0.93 versus $0.75, a 17.7 percent beat on the Zacks basis with revenue $3.12 billion missing by 13.5 percent; guidance $4.04–$4.16 reaffirmed; capital plan framed as '$70+ billion'; equity plan 85 percent complete
recentDevelopments.read: The financing risk of the base plan is largely retired; what remains open is the $10 billion-plus of line of sight that would take rate-base growth to ~13 percent.

recentDevelopments.headline: SPS proposes a second portfolio of 3,928 MW by 2030 — five solar, one solar-plus-storage, four wind and one natural gas project from more than 50 proposals
recentDevelopments.read: SPS is now carrying two overlapping build portfolios (5,168 MW from 2025 and 3,928 MW from 2026) against demand growth the company puts above 40 percent by 2030.

recentDevelopments.headline: Sherco Solar Phase 3 completes the 710 MW, 1.7-million-panel project; a Phase 4 to 910 MW by 2029 is proposed
recentDevelopments.read: The company's first owned large-scale solar is finished on the retiring coal site — the model for how Xcel wants to own the replacement fleet rather than buy it.

recentDevelopments.headline: CPR reports QTS's 177 MW Aurora, Colorado campus is Xcel's single largest customer, served by a $28 million 230 kV line, and is seeking permits for 98 more diesel backup generators
recentDevelopments.read: Xcel's largest existing load is a colocation campus, not a hyperscaler campus — the pipeline's 1 GW-plus projects would be an order of magnitude beyond anything on the system today.

recentDevelopments.headline: SPS is awarded a $113 million Texas Energy Fund Outside-ERCOT grant for pole inspections, Enhanced Powerline Safety Settings and line monitoring
recentDevelopments.read: Texas is now co-funding the hardening the AG's injunction requires — public money reduces the rate-case exposure of the wildfire spend.

recentDevelopments.headline: High Plains Solar + BESS in Morgan County, Colorado: 250 MW solar and 200 MW storage, $685 million, company-owned, built with Mortenson, in service December 2027
recentDevelopments.read: One of only two company-owned projects in the Colorado NTP — the EPC is named, which is rarer than it should be in Xcel's disclosures.

recentDevelopments.headline: Wisconsin Large Load Tariff filed with the PSCW (100 MW and above, 15-year commitments, 75 percent minimum demand, exit fees recovering all remaining infrastructure cost)
recentDevelopments.read: Third state, same architecture — Xcel is standardizing the contract before it standardizes the customer.

recentDevelopments.headline: Minnesota PUC verbally approves ~$211 million over two years for NSP-Minnesota at a 9.6 percent ROE (from 9.25 percent) on a 3–2 vote, about 60 percent less than the initial request
recentDevelopments.read: The ROE moved up but the dollars moved down; the Department of Commerce called the deal 'terrible ratepayer value', which is the political backdrop for every large-load filing in the state.

recentDevelopments.headline: 2025 Sustainability Report: carbon emissions down 58 percent from 2005, 27 coal units retired or converted, reliability 99.98 percent, electric bills 29 percent below the national average, ~11,500 employees
recentDevelopments.read: The affordability line — bills below the national average — is the argument Xcel will need in every 2026–2027 rate and tariff proceeding.

recentDevelopments.headline: Earthjustice, SWEEP and Rewiring America petition to intervene in the Colorado large-load tariff proceeding seeking 'stronger protections against shifting infrastructure costs onto existing customers'
recentDevelopments.read: Intervention by the clean-energy advocates, not the consumer advocate, is the tell: the argument is about who pays for the clean premium, not whether data centers come.

recentDevelopments.headline: Xcel establishes a $4.3 billion at-the-market equity distribution program with forward-sale capability
recentDevelopments.read: The vehicle that took the equity plan from 'roughly $1.5 billion issued' in Q1 to 85 percent complete by June 30.

recentDevelopments.headline: Minnesota PUC approves the 420 MW Lyon County Generating Station gas peaker for late 2028
recentDevelopments.read: Firm dispatchable capacity cleared in Minnesota without the combined-cycle plant Xcel had earlier proposed at Sherco — the IRP settlement's shape held.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q1 2026: ongoing EPS $0.91 matches the Zacks consensus; revenue $4.02 billion misses by 4.8 percent; guidance reaffirmed; Google agreement filed with the PUC with '$1.1 billion of benefits' claimed for customers
recentDevelopments.read: The first quarter in which the Google package was a filed proceeding rather than an announcement.

recentDevelopments.headline: Plant X Solar (150 MW) and Cunningham 1 Solar (72 MW plus a 36 MW battery) enter service in Texas as SPS's first owned solar; Cunningham 2 (196 MW) due April 2027
recentDevelopments.read: SPS's owned-generation build has started small; the 2,600 MW company-owned recommendation is the step change.

recentDevelopments.headline: Minnesota PUC approves Xcel's utility-owned 200 MW / $430 million distributed battery program (Capacity*Connect) over opposition from SEIA and Vote Solar
recentDevelopments.read: Distributed storage becomes rate base — the same ownership preference Xcel shows at utility scale, contested for the same reason.

recentDevelopments.headline: Colorado Large Load Tariff filed with the CPUC: 50 MW threshold, 15-year terms, 80 percent minimum demand, collateral and termination charges
recentDevelopments.read: The strictest of Xcel's three tariffs, filed in the state with the most contested rate record — decision expected early 2027.

recentDevelopments.headline: More than $130 million of nuclear production tax credit savings delivered to Upper Midwest customers ($330 million over two years), 'created under 2022 federal law; continued under 2025 law'
recentDevelopments.read: The company's own statement that the nuclear credit survived the 2025 reconciliation act — the wind and solar credits did not get the same sentence.

recentDevelopments.headline: Hemphill County court issues an agreed temporary injunction in the Texas AG's Smokehouse Creek suit: at least 35,000 pole inspections a year, tiered replacement deadlines, monthly compliance reports; trial set for April 19, 2027
recentDevelopments.read: SPS's distribution-hardening pace is now court-ordered rather than commission-approved, and the trial date sits inside the 2027 tariff-decision window.

recentDevelopments.headline: Google Pine Island: 1,900 MW of new clean energy and storage (1,400 MW wind, 200 MW solar, 300 MW / 30 GWh Form Energy iron-air) recovered through a Clean Energy Accelerator Charge; Google pays all grid costs and $50 million to Capacity*Connect
recentDevelopments.read: The first hyperscaler contract in the corpus that puts a named 100-hour battery into a customer charge — Xcel is selling a tariff design as much as power.

recentDevelopments.headline: Rob Cain named Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer, replacing Tim Peterson
recentDevelopments.read: Fourth executive-committee change in twelve months (Long, Sharp/Lamb, Shea, Cain) with the CEO and CFO unchanged.

recentDevelopments.headline: Colorado PUC approves up to 4,100 MW of Near-Term Procurement resources — ten projects of solar, storage, wind and gas — through an expedited process 'established to take advantage of expiring federal tax credits'
recentDevelopments.read: The commission's own language ties the approval to the federal credit deadline; the company's information sheet puts the captured benefit at $3 billion.

recentDevelopments.headline: Minnesota PUC approves the Mankato–Mississippi River line (~120 miles of 345 kV plus 20 miles of 161 kV)
recentDevelopments.read: Another CapX2020-corridor upgrade lands as MISO's Tranche 2.1 backbone moves toward certificate filings.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2025: ongoing EPS $3.80, inside guidance for the twenty-first year; base plan $60 billion for 2026–2030; 'contracted over 2 GW of new data centers'; more than 760 miles of 765 kV awarded
recentDevelopments.read: The plan that every 2026 filing is meant to fund.

recentDevelopments.headline: NextEra Energy MOU to co-develop generation, storage and transmission for large load across eight states; a joint development agreement for 2 GW of data-center capacity followed in April 2026
recentDevelopments.read: Xcel is renting a development machine rather than building one — the JDA's 'PPA, build-operate-transfer and self-build' menu keeps the assets regulated.

recentDevelopments.headline: GE Vernova Strategic Alliance: reservation for five F-class gas turbines, capacity reservation for 'multiple gigawatts' of wind turbines, synchronous condensers, running into the 2030s
recentDevelopments.read: Equipment was reserved before the Colorado or Wisconsin tariffs existed — supply is the constraint Xcel chose to solve first.

recentDevelopments.headline: Texas Attorney General Paxton sues SPS over the Smokehouse Creek fire, alleging poles 'nearly 100 years old' and seeking damages, civil penalties and a bar on recovering fire costs from customers
recentDevelopments.read: A state suit on top of private claims converts a settling liability into a political one — and it asks for the one remedy the rate case cannot give back.

recentDevelopments.headline: SPS signs a definitive Electric Service Agreement to supply up to 200 MW to Fermi America's Project Matador campus in Amarillo, 86 MW from January 2026 over a 115 kV system
recentDevelopments.read: The only named SPS data-center contract — and it is the smallest tier of the pipeline slide, in a state with no large-load tariff on file.

recentDevelopments.headline: Fitch affirms Xcel Energy at BBB+ and revises the outlook to stable from negative, noting FFO leverage 'at the downgrade threshold, leaving virtually no headroom'
recentDevelopments.read: Stable, with no headroom — which is why the equity plan was front-loaded.

recentDevelopments.headline: Xcel proposes the Upper Midwest's largest battery site: 600 MW at Sherco and 135.5 MW at Blue Lake in service late 2027, plus 200 MW more Sherco solar; the company intends to own all three
recentDevelopments.read: Storage doubled on the coal site — and the ownership preference is explicit.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q3 2025: ongoing EPS $1.24 misses the Zacks consensus of $1.31; $287 million Marshall Fire charge; 2026 guidance initiated at $4.04–$4.16; base plan raised to $60 billion with ~$7 billion of equity through 2030
recentDevelopments.read: The miss and the plan increase in the same release — the market was asked to look through the charge to the rate base.

recentDevelopments.headline: Bria Shea named President, Xcel Energy – Minnesota, North Dakota and South Dakota, reporting to the CEO
recentDevelopments.read: The executive who signed the Google release four months later; her prior role was regional planning and policy, which is the skill the CEAC proceeding needs.

recentDevelopments.headline: Siemens Energy to supply ten SGT6-5000F turbines and generators (2,088 MW) for Tolk Station and a new Gaines County peaker in Texas, first deliveries early 2026
recentDevelopments.read: The larger of Xcel's two turbine commitments is with Siemens, not GE Vernova — SPS's gas build is already equipment-secured.

recentDevelopments.headline: S&P revises Xcel's outlook to stable from negative after the Marshall settlement, with a downgrade trigger at FFO-to-debt below 13 percent or 'another significant wildfire'
recentDevelopments.read: The rating agencies priced Marshall as closed; Smokehouse Creek is the remaining trigger they named.

recentDevelopments.headline: Marshall Fire agreements in principle: ~$640 million, ~$350 million from insurance, nothing from customers, no admission of fault, on the eve of trial
recentDevelopments.read: The largest litigation overhang cleared at roughly 30 percent of the fire's $2 billion-plus economic loss — a benchmark the Texas plaintiffs and the AG will have read.

recentDevelopments.headline: Minnesota PUC unanimously approves expanded spent-fuel storage at Prairie Island (1,100 MW); NRC 20-year extension request planned for 2026
recentDevelopments.read: Nuclear life extension is the cheapest carbon-free capacity in the Upper Midwest plan and the least contested.

recentDevelopments.headline: SPS announces 521 MW of plant extensions and 17 new projects totaling 5,168 MW by 2030 (3,200 MW dispatchable and storage, 1,968 MW wind and solar) against demand growth of more than 40 percent by 2030
recentDevelopments.read: SPS becomes the group's growth engine on paper — its ~22 percent rate-base CAGR starts here.

recentDevelopments.headline: Ryan Long named EVP and Chief Legal and Compliance Officer as Rob Berntsen departs; Long keeps the Minnesota presidency pending a search
recentDevelopments.read: Legal leadership changed three months before the Marshall settlement and six months before the Texas AG suit.

recentDevelopments.headline: Colorado PUC approves the 2025–2027 Wildfire Mitigation Plan settlement (~$1.9 billion), tripling AI cameras and formalizing PSPS
recentDevelopments.read: The plan's ~$9-a-month bill impact is the number Colorado's data-center opponents cite alongside every large-load filing.

recentDevelopments.headline: Scott Sharp becomes EVP and Chief Generation Officer and Michael Lamb EVP and Chief Delivery Officer as COO Tim O'Connor retires; the COO role is split
recentDevelopments.read: Generation and delivery now report separately to the CEO — the build program and the wildfire program each get an executive owner.

recentDevelopments.headline: Minnesota PUC approves the Upper Midwest Energy Plan: 3,430 MW wind, 550 MW solar, 600 MW storage by 2030, the Lyon County peaker, all coal retired by 2030 and an 80-percent-plus carbon reduction
recentDevelopments.read: The resource plan that the Google package sits on top of — 1,900 MW more, outside the plan, on one contract.

recentDevelopments.headline: SPP awards Xcel the first 765 kV line in its footprint (Potter–Crossroads–Phantom, Amarillo to Lea County) plus two smaller lines
recentDevelopments.read: The transmission that makes Panhandle-scale load physically possible, in service Q2 2031.

recentDevelopments.headline: Harrington Generating Station (1,018 MW, Amarillo) completes its conversion from coal to natural gas
recentDevelopments.read: SPS's coal exit runs through conversion rather than retirement — capacity is kept on the system.

recentDevelopments.headline: NRC grants Monticello a 20-year subsequent license renewal to 2050
recentDevelopments.read: Sixty years of licence for the smallest unit in the fleet; Prairie Island follows in 2026.

recentDevelopments.headline: Colorado Just Transition Solicitation Phase 1 filed to replace the remaining coal plants, forecasting 5,000–14,000 MW of new capacity for 2028–2031 on 3–7 percent annual sales growth
recentDevelopments.read: A 5–14 GW range is the width of the data-center uncertainty in one filing.

recentDevelopments.headline: Utility Dive: Xcel reports 6.7 GW of data-center project requests with confirmed interest from Meta and Microsoft in Minnesota and QTS in Colorado; 'nearly half' of growth now from tech companies
recentDevelopments.read: The earliest public sizing of the queue — the 20 GW-plus figure of 2026 is three times this.

relationships.context: The company's February 23, 2026 release states the agreement 'will provide for 1,400 MW of wind, 200 MW of solar and 300 MW of long-duration energy storage, along with a $50 million investment towards Xcel Energy's Capacity*Connect Program', that Google will cover new grid infrastructure costs, and that the ESA requires MPUC approval. The Q2 2026 8-K adds the counterparty name (Echo Zone, LLC, a Google subsidiary), the April 2026 filing date and the claim of approximately $1.1 billion of customer benefits. Utility Dive quotes CEO Frenzel calling the deal the template for the company's large-load tariff strategy. The comment period closes September 8, 2026 with a decision expected in early 2027; the relationship is recorded as announced rather than active because the ESA is not yet approved.

relationships.note: NSP-Minnesota supplies Meta's Rosemount data center under three ESAs the Minnesota PUC approved in October 2023; Meta pays for its transmission upgrades per the company.
relationships.context: The company's March 15, 2024 story states Meta is investing more than $800 million at UMore Park with about 1,000 construction and 100 permanent jobs, that 'Meta pays transmission upgrades', and that the supply agreement was approved by the MPUC. KSTP and the Star Tribune reported the October 2023 approval of three ESAs for a $700 million facility at a discounted rate. Utility Dive's August 2024 report listed Meta among the confirmed interests in Xcel's 6.7 GW queue. This is the only hyperscaler contract on the system that is both approved and in service.

Utility Dive's August 2024 report named QTS as a confirmed Colorado interest in the queue. The 'since' year is the queue disclosure, not a contract date, which the sources do not give.

relationships.note: Xcel sold Microsoft 295 acres near its Becker, Minnesota Sherco site for a data center, per the Star Tribune; Microsoft was a confirmed interest in the 2024 queue per Utility Dive. No ESA, tariff filing or load figure has been published, so the link is recorded as a land sale rather than a supply relationship.
relationships.context: The Star Tribune reports that 'Xcel sold 295 acres near Becker to Microsoft' alongside a 348-acre sale to Elk River Technologies; Utility Dive's August 5, 2024 article lists Microsoft among the companies with 'confirmed interest' in Xcel's 6.7 GW of data-center requests in Minnesota. Neither source states a signed electric service agreement, and Xcel's own channels do not name Microsoft as a customer. Collection gap: whether Microsoft is one of the undisclosed contracts on the company's pipeline slide cannot be established from public sources.

relationships.context: The Star Tribune describes Amazon's retreat as the 'latest gut punch for Becker', the town hosting Xcel's Sherco site and the Microsoft parcel. The episode is recorded because it is the one public case of a hyperscaler leaving Xcel's queue, and because it happened in the session that produced Minnesota's data-center cost-protection law. No Xcel first-party source names Amazon.

relationships.via: Joint development agreement — generation, storage and interconnection for large load

The Q1 2026 investor slides, per Investing.com, describe the JDA as 'co-developing generation solutions for 2 GW of data center capacity, with plans to expand' using 'a mix of power purchase agreements, build-operate-transfer arrangements, and self-build projects'. RTO Insider quotes Frenzel on combining the two companies' sales, development and analytical teams. Registered here against the NextEra Energy Resources slug because the development counterparty is NextEra's competitive arm; the corporate signatory is NextEra Energy, Inc.

policyExposure.regime: Large-load tariffs (Minnesota approved; Colorado and Wisconsin filed)
policyExposure.exposure: Minnesota's Large Load Tariff (Proceeding M-25-289) is approved for customers of 100 MW and above with a 15-year minimum term and a 75 percent minimum demand charge, and Minnesota's 2025 law layers annual fees of $2–5 million per large customer into an efficiency account. Colorado's proposed tariff (26AL-0137E, 50 MW, 80 percent minimum demand) and Wisconsin's (4220-TE-119, 100 MW, 75 percent) await decisions in early 2027. SPS has no large-load tariff on file in Texas or New Mexico.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company's stated contract principles: recover capital investment, protect existing customers from stranded-asset risk, contractual risk avoidance, and 15-year-plus terms with minimum bills, collateral and exit fees equal to the minimum bill over the lesser of the remaining term or ten years.

policyExposure.regime: Federal clean-energy credits after the 2025 reconciliation act (IRA wind/solar phase-out, 45U nuclear, transferability)
policyExposure.exposure: The company's financing plan carries the footnote 'Financing plans reflect tax credit transferability and are subject to change', its 2025 ongoing EPS bridge credits PTCs with +$0.23, and it framed Colorado's Near-Term Procurement as capturing '$3 billion in federal tax benefits' before credits expire; the Colorado PUC's own release describes the expedited process as 'established to take advantage of expiring federal tax credits'. Under the 2025 law, wind and solar must begin construction by July 4, 2026 or be placed in service by December 31, 2027 to qualify, per Stoel Rives; storage credits are unaffected. Nuclear production credits continue — 'created under 2022 federal law; continued under 2025 law' per the company's March 2026 release.
policyExposure.mitigation: Company-stated: safe-harbored equipment for '~20 GW renewable generation and storage' per POWER's account of the February 2026 investor materials; the Colorado NTP timed to the deadline; continued pass-through of nuclear credits ($330 million over two years).

policyExposure.regime: Wildfire liability law — Texas, North Dakota, South Dakota reforms; no Colorado statute; Colorado securitization
policyExposure.exposure: The company's May 2026 investor deck states that tort-reform legislation 'passed in Texas, North Dakota, and South Dakota with standard of care / prudence if following approved plan', and lists a federal liability backstop and state backstop funds as unfinished agenda items. No Colorado wildfire-liability statute is cited; Colorado's exposure is instead managed through the approved $1.9 billion Wildfire Mitigation Plan with 'a securitization mechanism for up to $1.2 billion' and a planned 2029 securitization. S&P's September 2025 outlook revision named 'another significant wildfire' as a downgrade trigger.
policyExposure.mitigation: Company-stated: the Colorado and Texas mitigation plans, PSPS programs, ~$5 billion of wildfire capital in the 2026–2030 plan, and its stated legislative agenda for a federal fund and state backstops.

policyExposure.regime: Texas Attorney General litigation and agreed injunction (Smokehouse Creek)
policyExposure.exposure: The State of Texas sued SPS on December 16, 2025 seeking damages, civil penalties of '$1 million or more' and an order barring Xcel 'from recovering fire costs from customers'. The February 2026 agreed temporary injunction requires SPS to 'inspect no fewer than 35,000 poles annually', replace high-risk poles within 24 hours, 5 days or 35 days by tier, file monthly compliance reports, and not claim its Texas distribution system poses no fire risk; trial is set for April 19, 2027.
policyExposure.mitigation: Company-stated: SPS 'disputes claims that we acted negligently'; the August 2026 Texas Wildfire Mitigation Plan filing and the $113 million Texas Energy Fund grant fund the inspection and replacement program.

policyExposure.regime: State clean-energy mandates — Minnesota 100% carbon-free by 2040; Colorado 80% by 2030 and coal exit; New Mexico RPS
policyExposure.exposure: Minnesota requires 100 percent carbon-free electricity by 2040 and the company states 'large load additions will not interfere with our ability to meet these goals'; Colorado requires an 80 percent carbon reduction by 2030 with Comanche 3 retiring by January 1, 2031; New Mexico requires 50 percent renewable by 2030, 80 percent by 2040 and 100 percent carbon-free by 2045. The company's own target is out of coal by the end of 2030 with an 80-percent-plus (up to 88 percent) reduction in the Upper Midwest by 2030.
policyExposure.mitigation: Company-stated: the Upper Midwest Energy Plan, the Colorado Clean Energy Plan and Just Transition Solicitation, and the Google CEAC structure that adds clean resources on the customer's account.

policyExposure.regime: State rate regulation — 2026 base-rate outcomes and ROE contests
policyExposure.exposure: Colorado approved ~$157 million of a $356 million electric request in August 2026 (ROE 9.3 percent, equity 54.5 percent per the settlement); Minnesota approved ~$211 million over two years at 9.6 percent on a 3–2 vote now under reconsideration petitions; Wisconsin set 9.8 percent; New Mexico's stipulation is at 9.5 percent pending a Q4 2026 decision. Commissioner Blank's August 2026 statement on capital spending growing 'considerably faster than inflation' is on the record in the state with the largest rate base.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Xcel's data-center growth is gated by commission decisions rather than by demand or by equipment. Basis: the company's own slide shows ~2 GW contracted against more than 20 GW of pipeline and states it expects only ~1 GW signed in 2026; the Colorado and Wisconsin tariffs, the Google CEAC and the SPS portfolio certificates all decide in late 2026 or early 2027, and only Minnesota's tariff is approved. The contracted figure did not move between the Q1 and Q2 2026 decks.

(High confidence) We assess that the company has deliberately bought supply optionality ahead of load: five GE Vernova F-class turbines inside twelve gas-turbine reservations, ten Siemens Energy turbines (2,088 MW), multi-gigawatt wind reservations and a 2 GW NextEra joint development agreement were all executed before any tariff outside Minnesota was approved. This is the right sequence for a turbine market with multi-year lead times and the wrong one if commissions slow — the risk is reserved slots without certificated projects, which the company would carry as line-of-sight capital rather than base plan.

(High confidence) We assess that wildfire has moved from a litigation variable to a financing variable. Marshall closed at $640 million with $353 million of insurance and no customer recovery; Smokehouse Creek stands at a $503 million estimate the company says it cannot cap, against a $525 million policy with about $80 million left; S&P and Fitch both returned to stable in late 2025 but named a further fire and FFO-to-debt below 13 percent as triggers, and Fitch describes 'virtually no headroom'. The equity plan being 85 percent complete is the company's answer, and it is a good one for the base plan only.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that Southwestern Public Service is simultaneously the group's growth engine and its unmanaged risk. Basis: SPS carries a ~22 percent rate-base CAGR, 4.8 percent year-to-date sales growth, $19 billion of the base plan and two overlapping build portfolios — and also the Smokehouse Creek liability, a Texas Attorney General suit set for trial in April 2027, an agreed injunction dictating pole-replacement pace, no large-load tariff in either state, and an interim president since March 2026 with no explanatory release. Collection gap: who runs SPS on a permanent basis, and why the change occurred, is not established from public sources.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that regulatory friction on base rates is rising at exactly the moment the plan needs ~11 percent rate-base growth, and that the company's response is to route growth through riders and customer-specific charges rather than through rate cases. Basis: Colorado cut a settled $225 million case to $157 million with a commissioner warning about capital growth; Minnesota's 3–2 order is under reconsideration; the 2025 EPS bridge shows riders contributing more than twice what rate cases did. The CEAC and the large-load tariffs are the same instinct applied to data centers — the test is whether commissions accept it at 1,900 MW on one contract.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the ownership share of the replacement fleet, not its size, is where Xcel's earnings leverage lies. Basis: Colorado's NTP awarded 2 company-owned projects against 9 PPAs, while SPS recommends ~70 percent company-owned and the Upper Midwest plan uses build-own-transfer wind; the company intends to own the Sherco and Blue Lake batteries and the Capacity*Connect fleet. Every solicitation outcome should be read as an ownership ratio first.

(Low confidence) We assess that the Google package is Xcel's bid to be the tariff designer of record for hyperscalers in MISO — a customer-funded 1,900 MW clean-energy build with a 100-hour iron-air battery. The evidence is one unapproved contract; whether other hyperscalers will accept full incremental cost plus a clean premium, and whether the Minnesota PUC approves 1,900 MW outside a resource plan, are both untested. Trade press supports the template framing; no second signatory does.

INDICATORS TO WATCH — September 8, 2026: Minnesota comment period closes on the Google ESA/CEAC; a decision in early 2027 approving 1,900 MW on one contract would confirm Judgment 7. Mid-October 2026: Minnesota PUC response to the reconsideration petitions on the 9.6 percent ROE. Q4 2026: New Mexico decision (rates in December), Colorado gas decision, PSCo Just Transition RFP issuance, NSP renewable RFP recommendation; company-owned share in each is the number to read. Late October 2026: Q3 results — whether the contracted block finally moves above ~2 GW and whether a fifth disclosed contract is named. Early 2027: Colorado and Wisconsin large-load tariff decisions; SPS certificates for the 2026 portfolio. April 19, 2027: Texas AG trial; a judgment barring customer recovery of fire costs would change the SPS credit story more than any mitigation spend. Any Colorado wildfire-liability statute would remove the one liability regime the company lists as unaddressed.
